messages.subject: generic model
parts:
Hi Folks, 

I have tried running a model with two factors in the "generic" list. As the factor are somewhat related (additive and dominance kinship matrices), even using "em" there are problems in convergence. 

Thus, I wondering define the initial values for components of variance. How could I do it?

Thanks,

messages.author: 37c4b6bc71d5d203
messages.subject: Re: [breedR] generic model
parts:
Dear Roberto,

See the argument |var.ini| of |remlf90()| in the help (|?remlf90|).

Here is a reproducible example with a valid specification of the initial
variances within the generic components:

|# Dummy fit: just to retrieve incidence and covariance matrices rdummy
<- remlf90( fixed = phe_X ~ 1, genetic = list( model = 'add_animal',
pedigree = globulus[, 1:3], id = 'self', var.ini = 10 ), spatial = list(
model = 'blocks', coord = globulus[, c('x','y')], id = 'bl', var.ini = 1
), var.ini = list(resid = 5), data = globulus ) # Same model with
generic components res <- remlf90( fixed = phe_X ~ 1, generic = list( ##
genetic add = with( rdummy$effects$genetic$effects$direct,
list(incidence.matrix, structure.matrix, var.ini = 10) ), ## spatial bl
= with( rdummy$effects$spatial$effects$blocks, list(incidence.matrix,
structure.matrix, var.ini = 1) ) ), var.ini = list(resid = 5), data =
globulus ) |

Best wishes

ƒacu.-

messages.subject: Re: [breedR] generic model
parts: Sorry, the code went unreadable. Here it goes again.

# Dummy fit: just to retrieve incidence and covariance matrices
rdummy <- remlf90(
  fixed   = phe_X ~ 1,
  genetic = list(
    model    = 'add_animal',
    pedigree = globulus[, 1:3],
    id       = 'self',
    var.ini = 10
  ),
  spatial = list(
    model = 'blocks',
    coord = globulus[, c('x','y')],
    id    = 'bl',
    var.ini = 1
  ),
  var.ini = list(resid = 5),
  data    = globulus
)


# Same model with generic components
res <- remlf90(
  fixed  = phe_X ~ 1,
  generic = list(
    ## genetic
    add = with(
      rdummy$effects$genetic$effects$direct,
      list(incidence.matrix, structure.matrix, var.ini = 10)
    ),
    ## spatial
    bl = with(
      rdummy$effects$spatial$effects$blocks,
      list(incidence.matrix, structure.matrix, var.ini = 1)
    )
  ),
  var.ini = list(resid = 5),
  data   = globulus
)
